results.text: The current history also led to a direct check of I72 §7 through its ending: its bounded-activity comparison uses extreme state weights and Dirichlet-form comparison for a weighted switch chain. E126 instead averages symmetric independent log-odds perturbations of an arbitrary finite law. That distinction does not elevate it above the technical contribution category shared by both comparisons.

The log-concave sampling source assumes C² potentials with supplied minimizer 0, `V(0)=0`, `I≤∇²V≤2I`, an exact value-and-gradient oracle, measurable random real operations and **unrestricted between-query computation**. For every fixed ε>0 it pays an every-execution `C_ε d^ε` query cap and TV≤1/10; it also pays a logarithmic query lower bound. Its complete final conditional descent, ideal-history error summation, Gaussian base rule, fixed caps and finite-dimensional fallback were read. Finite implementation of recursively noisy means is already an explicit lower operation, not an assumed sampling oracle. This is not a polynomial bit-time theorem, nor does it grant finite oracle precision robustness. No computational guarantee or precision impossibility is nominated from this distinction.

Read *An FPRAS for Common Integer Polymatroid Bases with Binary Capacities*, `build/sections/introduction.tex`, blob `c74bce3869be3469749091b6f3ab60dbf61a81fa`, `thm:main`: for normalized monotone integral submodular r1,r2 with equal total rank R, count exactly once each nonnegative integer x with `x(E)=R`, `x(S)≤ri(S)` for every S and i. Runtime is polynomial in ground-set size, binary input length, ε^-1 and log δ^-1 on every execution; zero counts are detected exactly. Its matroid and cell-bounded contingency-table companions were checked. The matroid paper's `cor:intersection` already covers all, prescribed-size, and maximum-size common independent sets, including unequal input ranks. Projection is not one of these changes of cardinality.

Relevant proof comparisons also include the matching paper's complete entropy/weighted sections, the cell-bounded table paper's binary and integer signature arguments and transport interface, and the exact-table companion's signature interface. `pinned-manifest.json` distinguishes all retained files from actual read passages in `read-passages.json`; retaining a paper is not represented as reading every auxiliary algorithm in it.

**Capacity improvements retain their hypotheses.** Schweitzer, [Capacity of Lorentzian polynomials, v2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.14406v2), Theorem 2.1 and its coefficient corollary, and Brändén–Leake–Pak, [Lower bounds for contingency tables via Lorentzian polynomials, v3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.05907v3), Theorems 5.10/5.11, give coefficient/capacity estimates for Lorentzian, denormalized Lorentzian, or stable polynomials. Their proofs reduce to bivariate coefficient estimates and iterate differentiation/specialization. Those closure premises need verification on the polynomial actually used. The four-element example in §5 fails log-concavity for the common-base polynomial, even though both individual matroid polynomials are stable. The source's two positive factorial lifts and their agreement on transversals are not a license to transfer either lift's signature to this polynomial.

I read AGENTS.md, the current ledger, I13/I19/I22/I25, and the I56/I58 contribution decisions. together with a polynomial comparison from weighted slice heat baths to the actual weighted switches. The identity with c=1 is the uniform source's aggregate result; it cannot simply be asserted with changed inner products. On even the two states of a four-vertex switch, unequal positive probabilities p and 1−p make the swap send an indicator of squared norm p to one of squared norm 1−p, so it is not an L² isometry. The source projection `(I−T_ab)/2` consequently loses its self-adjoint projection property. This invalidates that unchanged proof step, not the proposed uniform weighted inequality or W.
